title: Prompt diffing + lightweight prompt versioning (scratch)
content:
Goal:
quickly compare prompt edits, see diff, run A/B with old/new, rollback, and bake prompt versions into deployments (hosted/dedicated/private).

Problem notes (why):
- Engineers edit prompts inline in code or in Console; tiny changes cause large downstream quality/cost changes. Hard to track which prompt version served to which user.
- Current flow: copy/paste -> test -> push -> no structured history tied to model or route. No lightweight guardrails.
- Need: low-friction diffing + stable identifiers + ability to pin a prompt to a rollout.

Core idea (MVP):
- Prompt Library service (thin): stores prompt blobs with metadata: id (short hash), semantic title, tags, author, created_at, refs -> model variants / routes.
- Inline diff UI in Console + small CLI (redwood prompt diff <id1> <id2>).
- A/B run: attach two prompt ids to a route rollout (10% vs 90%) and capture telemetry.
- Rollback: choose previous prompt id and promote.

User stories:
- As an ML engineer, I want to see line-level diffs between two prompt versions so I can reason about behavioural changes.
- As a product engineer, I want to pin a prompt version to a route so a canary doesn't accidentally use latest master prompt.
- As an SRE/owner, I want to tie a prompt id to logs/trace so I can investigate regressions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Prompt library stores new prompt version via Console and API.
- Console shows side-by-side diff + token-length estimate + cost delta estimate (rough).
- Attach prompt id to existing route config and run small A/B split (server honors param).
- Telemetry: request-level metadata contains prompt_id; can filter traces by prompt_id in Console.

Implementation notes / open questions:
- Storage: small DB table keyed by prompt id (sha256 prefix), content as text. Do we need blob store? probably not for MVP.
- Prompt templating: support both static blobs and parameterized templates (templated variables -> show diff of template and of rendered sample?).
- Semantic diff vs textual diff: consider showing embeddings-based similarity for large prompts (quick indicator if change is minor).
- Cost estimator: use tokenizer local calc + model profile to estimate per-request delta. Might be off for streaming.
- Security: prompts may contain PII or secrets (rare) — restrict visibility, support redaction in UI. Integrate with audit logs.
- Backwards compatibility: existing API calls without prompt_id behave as now (system copies latest library prompt).

Integration with Redwood features:
- Console: new "Prompt library" view, search by tag/author.
- Rollouts: extend rollout object to include prompt_id binding per variant.
- Evals: ability to point an eval run at a specific prompt_id for regression tests.
- Private deployments: allow syncing prompt library to private control plane or export bundle.

Quick CLI sketch:
- redwood prompt save -t "small-rewrite" -m "assistant-rewrite" -f ./prompt.txt -> returns prompt_id
- redwood prompt diff idA idB --sample-inputs ./cases.json
- redwood route update --route payments-parse --prompt-id idA --rollout 0.2

UX sketches (notes to self):
- Diff pane: left old, right new, token counts above each, cost delta badge. Inline suggestions: highlight sub-phrases that change model instruction ("you are a helpful assistant" -> more prescriptive).
- Quick-run modal: pick sample set, run both prompts in parallel, show examples + metrics (BLEU-ish? embedding distance? hallucination count from heuristics).
- History view: chronological timeline of saves + commit message + who pinned to which route.

Metrics to track for feature success:
- time to rollback after regression (target < 10 min)
- number of prompts saved per week (adoption)
- fraction of production routes with pinned prompt ids (increase over time)
- reduction in token-cost variance after pinning (proxy)

Risks / concerns:
- UI complexity -> adoption friction. MVP must be tiny and obvious.
- Storage of many prompt versions could explode (but each prompt small). Add retention policy.
- Cross-compatibility with dynamic prompt generation (in-code templates). Might require instrumentation or SDK changes.

Next actions / TODOs:
- mock console wireframe (Kai)
- proto DB schema + minimal API (Mira)
- spike: token-cost diff calc using existing model profiles (me)
- write a short RFC for infra + rollout attachment (link: JIRA INF-2145)
- quick user interviews with 3 infra / ML engineers to validate painpoints

Notes-to-self:
- think about tying prompt_id into request-level sampling headers so SREs can query by id.
- consider prompt 'tags' like safety-reviewed, experimental, canary.
- small UX: "save as draft" vs "publish" concept.

Random brain fragments:
- Could implement as git-like flow (commit / tag / revert) but keep hidden complexity — present simple "save" + id.
- Embedding diff: show cosine change across sample outputs. Might help quantify semantic drift.

End of scratch.
